headline_marked: [[India's Telegram ban]] causes 49% surge in VPN app downloads, biggest since 2025
headline: India's Telegram ban causes 49% surge in VPN app downloads, biggest since 2025
summary: Following a week-long restriction on Telegram over exam fraud concerns, major VPN app downloads in India jumped 49% in a single day, the biggest spike since early 2025.
details: India's temporary restriction on the messaging app Telegram led to a significant increase in VPN and alternative app downloads. On the day the ban was announced, major VPN app downloads rose 49% to 208,000, marking the biggest daily surge since early 2025.

Specific VPN services saw massive spikes, with Proton VPN downloads jumping 113% on iOS and 64% on Google Play. Turbo VPN also recorded an 85% increase on iOS and 35% on Google Play, pushing these services up India's app-store charts.

Beyond app downloads, VPN registrations soared, with Proton reporting a 120% increase in daily sign-ups from India. Windscribe also saw signups peak 100% above baseline, a trend consistent with user behavior in regions facing app bans or internet restrictions.

Users also explored alternative messaging apps. Signal downloads rose 72% on iOS and 322% on Google Play, while Viber downloads increased 216%. The Telegram-linked app iMe saw its Google Play downloads surge from a daily average of 827 to 50,900.

Despite the restrictions, Telegram's daily active users in India actually rose 17% on the day the measure was announced. This suggests users were actively trying to circumvent the ban, further supported by a sharp increase in DNS requests for Telegram domains.

The Indian government imposed the temporary ban until June 22 to prevent the spread of fake exam papers for a re-test. Telegram has challenged the order in the Delhi High Court, arguing for content-specific targeting instead of a platform-wide restriction affecting over 150 million users.

headline: AltStore PAL now available in Brazil as Apple enables alternative app marketplaces
summary: Brazilian iPhone users can now access alternative app marketplaces, with AltStore PAL leading the charge. This marks a significant shift in Apple's app distribution policy for the region.
details: Brazilian iPhone users can now download AltStore PAL, marking the first time Apple has officially enabled alternative app marketplaces in the country. This move expands app distribution options beyond the traditional App Store.
